title: How to Check a Credit Repair Company Before You Pay
h1: How to Check a Credit Repair Company Before You Pay
meta_description: Learn how to check a credit repair company using contract terms, upfront fee rules, complaints, state regulators, and warning signs.
primary_question: How do I check a credit repair company?
questions_answered: How do I check a credit repair company?
What are credit repair red flags?
Can a credit repair company charge upfront fees?
Where can I complain about a credit repair company?

sections.heading: Short Answer
sections.content: Before paying a credit repair company, check its legal name, contract terms, cancellation rights, complaint history, state requirements, and whether it promises results it cannot control. Be especially careful with upfront payment demands, guaranteed score claims, and advice to dispute accurate information.

sections.heading: Confirm the Company and Contract
sections.content: A legitimate credit repair company should clearly identify its legal name, address, services, pricing, timeline, cancellation rights, and what it will and will not do. Read the agreement before paying or sharing sensitive information.

sections.heading: Know the Upfront Fee Warning
sections.content: Federal credit repair rules restrict charging consumers before promised services are performed. If a company demands payment before doing the work it promised, that is a major warning sign and a reason to review official FTC guidance.

sections.heading: Watch for Risky Promises
sections.content: Be careful with companies that guarantee a specific score increase, claim they can remove accurate negative information, tell you to create a new credit identity, or pressure you to sign immediately. Credit repair cannot legally erase accurate and timely credit report information just because it is negative.

sections.heading: Check Complaints and Regulators
sections.content: Review complaint patterns through official complaint resources and identify the state regulator or attorney general office that handles credit repair or consumer protection issues in your state. If a company operates nationally, check whether complaint themes repeat across states.

sections.heading: Compare Against Free Rights
sections.content: You can dispute inaccurate credit report information yourself. Paying for help may be useful for some consumers, but the company should explain what it does beyond the free dispute rights you already have.

faq_schema.question: How do I check a credit repair company?
faq_schema.answer: Confirm the legal name, contract terms, cancellation rights, complaint history, state regulator context, and whether the company avoids guaranteed score claims or upfront-fee red flags.

faq_schema.question: Can credit repair companies guarantee results?
faq_schema.answer: No company can guarantee that accurate negative information will be removed or that your score will increase by a specific amount.

faq_schema.question: Can I repair credit myself?
faq_schema.answer: Yes. Consumers can dispute inaccurate credit report information directly. A paid company should clearly explain what extra service it provides.

faq_schema.question: Where can I complain about a credit repair company?
faq_schema.answer: Depending on the issue, you may use the CFPB, FTC, state attorney general, or state consumer credit regulator. Keep written records and copies of the contract.
